samples.summary: New `data-text-edit-keepalive` exemption is keyed on a static attribute, so focus is permanently stranded on a picker trigger when its popup is dismissed by Esc / outside-click — the canvas keyboard stays dead, which is the exact #882 state the hook exists to fix
samples.evidence: `isReleasable()` now returns false for any button under `[data-text-edit-keepalive]` (line 76). The exemption assumes such a control only ever holds focus while the text box will get it back, but the shared pickers only refocus the editor on a *swatch click*: `useMenuCloseHandlers(() => editor?.focus())` (text-format-group.tsx:131) and `menu-focus.ts:52-57` early-return unless `swatchClickedRef` is set, documented as "Outside-click and Esc fall through to Radix's default focus-to-trigger" (menu-focus.ts:27-29). Concrete path on the board this delta newly opts in: enter a sticky's text edit → click "Text color" (`data-text-edit-keepalive`, text-format-group.tsx:245) → press Escape. Radix closes the popover and restores focus to the trigger `<button>`; the text box is still mounted (docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:748 skipped the blur-commit) but its textarea is not focused, and the hook now refuses to release. From that state every slides rule is gated off by `!isEditableTarget(e.target)` (keyboard.ts:218, 242, and Escape-to-exit), and typing goes nowhere — the user must click the canvas twice (the first click is eaten by the modal popover overlay). A live-session check (e.g. only exempt while `textEditor.isEditing()` *and* the popup is still open / focus is about to return) would keep the anti-Delete protection without stranding focus.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: toolbar-focus-release.ts:76 exempts anything under [data-text-edit-keepalive] from release, keyed only on the static attribute with no live-session/popup-open check. menu-focus.ts:52-57 refocuses the editor only when a swatch was clicked; Esc/outside-click fall through to Radix's default focus-to-trigger (documented at menu-focus.ts:27-29). The path is reachable: board-toolbar.tsx:137,186 opts the root into data-canvas-toolbar and renders TextEditSection (436-441) -> TextFormatGroup, whose "Text color" trigger is a plain <button> with data-text-edit-keepalive inside a modal Popover (text-format-group.tsx:239-255, color-swatch-button.tsx:34 has no mousedown preventDefault); slides toolbar/index.tsx:70,110 is identical. After Esc, focus sits on that button while the text box stays mounted (text-box-editor.ts:747-751 skips the blur commit), and every slides rule is gated off because isEditableTarget treats a focused BUTTON as editable (keyboard.ts:882, used at 218, 242, 131, ...). No other code refocuses the textarea — the only focusin listener in src is the hook itself (toolbar-focus-release.ts:127) — and pointerDriven is only cleared by Tab (line 104), so no alternative release fires. The existing tests encode the gap: keepalive keeps focus (test 85-93) while the Escape-release test only covers a non-keepalive menu (95-101). No guard, caller, or refocus path refutes it.

finding.summary: Focus release fires while a slides text-box edit session is still alive (keepalive path), re-arming destructive canvas shortcuts against the element being edited
finding.evidence: The hook is mounted on the whole slides `<Toolbar>` (index.tsx:110), including the `text-edit` contextual section. The docs text-box editor deliberately keeps the edit session mounted when focus moves from the textarea to a control tagged `data-text-edit-keepalive` (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:736-751: "skip the commit so the text-box stays mounted, and the control's own handler re-focuses via api.focus()"). For dropdown-style keepalive controls the re-focus only happens on the *swatch/item-selected* path — `useMenuCloseHandlers` (menu-focus.ts:52-57) explicitly lets Escape / outside-dismiss fall through to Radix's default focus-to-trigger without calling `editor.focus()`. In that state focus sits on the keepalive trigger `<button>`, which is exactly what `isEditableTarget()` (packages/slides/.../interactions/keyboard.ts:882) relied on to suppress the document-level rules. `isReleasable()` has no text-edit guard, so line 104 blurs that button to `document.body`; the slides keydown listener is bound to `document` unconditionally (editor.ts:2727) so with target=body the Delete/Backspace rule (keyboard.ts:215-231) now removes the element the user is still editing, and the printable-key type-to-edit rule (keyboard.ts:663-679) re-enters edit mode with `initialText`. Uncommitted text plus the whole element can be destroyed by one Delete press.

verdict.reason: The finding's central assertion — "isReleasable() has no text-edit guard" — is false in this repository. toolbar-focus-release.ts:71-79 defines isReleasable() with the clause `el.closest(TEXT_EDIT_KEEPALIVE_SELECTOR) === null` (line 76), where TEXT_EDIT_KEEPALIVE_SELECTOR = "[data-text-edit-keepalive]" (line 43). The only release site is line 121 (`if (isReleasable(document.activeElement)) releaseFocusToBody();`), so focus parked on a keepalive control is never blurred to body. The cited "line 104 blurs that button" is actually `if (e.key === "Tab") pointerDriven = false;`. The keepalive attribute is placed on the trigger elements themselves (text-paragraph-group.tsx:82, font-family-picker.tsx:133, text-format-group.tsx:245/340) or their immediate wrapper (font-size-picker.tsx:145), so `closest()` matches in exactly the Escape / outside-dismiss "Radix returns focus to the trigger" state the finding describes. The slides text-edit contextual section (text-edit-section.tsx:65-89) is composed only of those tagged controls plus the "Done" button, which intentionally exits text editing. A dedicated test (toolbar-focus-release.test.tsx:85-93) asserts focus is retained on a keepalive control after a pointer-driven click. The described code is not present as described and the described destructive path is unreachable.
